messages:
maya: Heads up — I noticed the workspace dropdown showing a different customer's workspace when I opened the routing policy editor :eyes:
jonathan: can you repro and share a screenshot?
maya: https://screens.redwood/internal/2026/console-snap (staging snapshot)
maya: repro steps: Console -> Projects -> Select tenant A -> Integrations -> Routing -> Edit -> workspace dropdown shows tenant B entries
sree: this sounds like potential data exposure. severity?
maya: not seeing API keys, but display names and a few tags are visible. still sensitive.
jonathan: which env did you hit? staging or prod?
maya: hit staging first, then noticed same pattern on prod for two orgs (low traffic).
jonathan: pulling console-service logs for the trace, pls paste trace id if you have it
maya: trace: abc123-console-20260315
jonathan: looking at logs: request to /api/v1/console/routing/edit returned cached payload. cache resolver logged tenant=null for some requests
jonathan: quick glance at code: cache key is built as `req.path + JSON.stringify(params)` — doesn't include tenant_id
ralph: that's a collision. different tenants can read the same cached UI payload if path/params match.
sree: confirmed locally: repro by replaying two different tenant sessions, same cache key reused. This is P0 for visibility leak.
jonathan: mitigation options: (1) include tenant_id in cache key, (2) partition cache by namespace, (3) on deploy flush affected keys. I can draft a patch for (1).
ralph: prefer (2) long-term but (1) is the fastest fix. also need to purge existing cache entries to avoid immediate exposure.
sree: plan: hotfix (1) + cache flush + canary deploy. assign owners: jonathan => patch & deploy, ralph => cache flush script + coord, maya => UI verification, sree => incident lead + postmortem.
deploy-bot: Started deploy of console-service:v2026.3-tenant-cache-fix to staging by jonathan
jonathan: pushed patch to include tenant_id in cache key and added unit test to assert tenant key present. staging deploy in progress.
maya: verifying staging now — dropdown shows only the selected workspace (no cross-tenant entries) :thumbsup:
jonathan: scheduling prod canary at 15:00 UTC. will run 10% for 30m then scale. rollback plan: revert image + immediate cache flush.
sree: add telemetry: emit metric `console.dropdown.cross_tenant_hits` when a dropdown returns entries not scoped to requester; alert if >0 in prod. Also add `tenant_cache_miss_rate` for monitoring.
jonathan: added debug log that prints the cache key for 1% of requests to help validate key contents during canary.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy to prod (10%) started by jonathan
maya: monitoring canary nodes, no cross-tenant dropdowns observed so far.
jonathan: rolling to 100% now
deploy-bot: Deploy succeeded to 100% at 15:22 UTC
sree: good. ralph, did cache flush run?
ralph: ran `redis-cli KEYS "console:*" | xargs -n100 redis-cli DEL` against cache cluster during the canary window. verified affected keys gone.
jonathan: follow-ups: expand unit tests to ensure tenant_id required for any UI cache key, add e2e test that simulates two tenants hitting dropdowns concurrently, audit other caches (session-cache, quicksearch-cache).
sree: I'll own postmortem and detection gap. creating page for timeline and root cause analysis.
maya: filed internal ticket INF-934 with links to timeline and logs: https://issues.redwood/INF-934
jonathan: thanks everyone. small ask: add code lint rule to fail builds when cache key uses request-scope values without tenant/context.
ralph: noted. I'll add an architectural note and sweep other cache usages this week.
sree: thanks Maya for catching this early. we'll close once postmortem and fixes are in main and telemetry is green.
maya: thanks all :heart:
